title: The mixed ramified-extension and quotient-reduction square
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $X,V,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, $f:V\to X$ separated of finite type, and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a closed immersion [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On ordinary small etale derived categories use $Rf_{*,R}$, $G_R=Ri_R^!$ right adjoint to $i_{*,R}$, and $\omega_R=a_{X,R}^{\times}R$, where $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a_{X,R}^{\times}$ is right adjoint to the compact-support functor defined by a fixed compactification [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, lem-exc-closed-ambient, def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $H_R(K,M)=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)$ and $D_RK=H_R(K,\omega_R)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing].

Let $E\subset L$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_L$, uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$, and ramification index $e\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For $1\le m\le n$ put $A_t=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^t$, $B_t=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_E^t\mathcal O_L=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^{et}$ for $t=m,n$. The horizontal coefficient maps are $a_t:A_t\to B_t$ and the vertical ones are the quotient maps $q_A:A_n\to A_m$, $q_B:B_n\to B_m$. Assume the finite-free bases of $B_t/A_t$ are reductions of a single $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\mathcal O_L$. Put $R_A=-\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$, $R_B=-\otimes^L_{B_n}B_m$, and $T_t=-\otimes^L_{A_t}B_t$. There is a canonical identification
$$B_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m\cong B_m,\qquad R_BT_n\cong T_mR_A,$$
with balancing formula $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$ on K-flat representatives. For a coefficient map $a:R\to S$ put $T_a=-\otimes_R^LS$. Let $c_a:T_aRf_{*,R}\to Rf_{*,S}T_a$ be the extended inverse-image counit transpose; let $b_a:T_aG_R\to G_ST_a$ be the extended exceptional counit transpose using the inverse closed-direct-image comparison; and let $u_a:T_a\omega_R\to\omega_S$ be the extended structure-morphism compact-support counit transpose. The compact-support comparison is the proper projection comparison composed with open extension by zero. Let $v_a:T_aH_R(K,M)\to H_S(T_aK,T_aM)$ be the transpose of extended evaluation. Set $\beta_a=H_S(1,u_a)\circ v_{a;K,\omega_R}$ for Verdier duality. All these are the specified morphisms, with balanced tensor associators understood.

For bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs (on $V$ for direct image and on $X$ for the other operations), all five mixed reduction squares commute. Here finite Tor means a finite interval bounding tensor with every degree-zero module sheaf; bounded constructibility is [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. Explicitly, for $Q_R=Rf_{*,R},G_R$, or $D_R$ and the corresponding one-input map $h_a=c_a,b_a$, or $\beta_a$,
$$h_{q_B;T_nK}\circ R_B(h_{a_n;K})=h_{a_m;R_AK}\circ T_m(h_{q_A;K}).$$
For internal Hom the same equation holds with both inputs $K,M$ extended or reduced; for $u$ it holds with the coefficient unit reduced along the square. The vertical maps are exactly the quotient comparisons of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image, lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek, lem-coef-finite-dualizing, thm-coef-finite-hom, cor-coef-finite-verdier]; the etale closed map is the counit-defined recovery of [lem-coef-finite-etale-descent]. The squares preserve evaluation and its double-dual transpose. All dual inputs and dualizing objects appearing in the quotient comparisons are bounded constructible finite-Tor. The same square is asserted on the finite-coefficient pro-etale realization, using the transported exceptional functor [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], constructibility [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], and Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Put $d=q_Ba_n=a_mq_A:A_n\to B_m$ and $S=T_d$. The equality of ring maps is equality on the image of every element of $\mathcal O_E$. Apply the canonical derived pullback composition of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] to identity geometric morphisms with these coefficient maps. It identifies both $R_BT_n$ and $T_mR_A$ with $S$, compatibly with tensors and units. On flat-term K-flat representatives, [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] allows successive extension to compute these functors; the maps are multiplication of the coefficient factors. In particular $((p\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto p\otimes a b$ on the $A_m$ path, and $((p\otimes b_n)\otimes b_m)\mapsto p\otimes q_B(b_n)b_m$ on the $B_n$ path. Since $B_n$ is free over $A_n$, its degree-zero complex computes $B_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_m$; quotienting its reduced basis identifies this with $B_m$. Thus these are the stipulated balanced identifications, not choices of endpoint isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 1

proof.text: All four rings are allowable finite stages: $A_t=A_{E,t}$ and $B_t=A_{L,et}$, with $em\le en$. The horizontal functors preserve bounded constructibility and every Tor interval by [lem-sf-finite-free-derived-scalar-calculus]; the vertical ones do so by [lem-coef-finite-hom-domain-calculus], applied over $E$ and over $L$. For each of the four coefficients, [lem-weil-verdier-preservation-strata] applies to this separated finite-type $X/k$ and carries every finite-Tor constructible input to a finite-Tor constructible dual. Apply it also to the coefficient unit: $R\mathcal Hom_R(R_X,\omega_R)=\omega_R$, since Hom from the rank-one unit is identity. This proves that all $\omega_R$, duals, repeated duals and their reductions used below meet the quotient lemmas' input hypotheses; no smoothness or site-perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 2

proof.text: For direct image apply the successive-coefficient equation of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image] to the two chains $A_n\to B_n\to B_m$ and $A_n\to A_m\to B_m$. Every algebra in either chain is finite as a module over its predecessor, and the starting $K$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor on $V$. The two composites are therefore both $c_{d;K}$ under step 1. This is exactly the asserted $c$ square. The cited equation explicitly permits an intermediate ring not presented as $A_{E,r}$, so it applies to the first chain. It also applies with $f=i$ and with $f$ the proper map in the fixed compactification; these versions will be used below.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 3

proof.text: Write the fixed structure compactification as $X\xrightarrow j\overline X\xrightarrow p\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $F_R=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$. For an etale finite-Tor constructible $N$, exact $j_!$ is bounded constructible by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero] applied to its finitely many cohomology sheaves. Its Tor interval is unchanged: the projection identity $j_!(N\otimes^Lj^*W)=j_!N\otimes^LW$ of [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor], for degree-zero $W$, reduces this to exactness of $j_!$. Thus step 3 applies to $p$ and $j_!N$. Denote its coefficient projection by $c^p_a$ and the open scalar comparison by $z_a$. The compact comparison is $C_a=Rp_{*,S}(z_a)\circ c^p_a$. The successive-scalar identity for $z$ in the same open-tensor node and that for $c^p$ in step 3 give, by naturality, $C_b\circ T_bC_a=C_{ba}$ for each of our two coefficient chains. Hence the two mixed compact-support paths are the same $C_d$. Their inverses have the corresponding reversed equation. The horizontal maps are the same finite-sum normalized comparisons by [lem-sf-finite-free-image-comparison], and the vertical compact maps are the quotient tensor comparisons of [lem-fix-compact-support-coefficient-change].

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 4

proof.text:
For closed exceptional image let $I_R=i_{*,R}$ and write $c_a:T_aI_R\to I_ST_a$ for its ordinary coefficient comparison. By [lem-coef-finite-etale-descent], applied also with equal quotient levels to type $G_RK$, the objects $G_RK$, its quotient reduction, and $G_ST_aK$ in a vertical comparison are bounded constructible finite-Tor, and the etale vertical $b$ is the specified exceptional-counit transpose. Horizontal $b$ is the same counit construction by [lem-sf-finite-free-exceptional-mate]. For any one of the two chains $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b U$, [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] applied to the inverse $c$ squares says the transpose of $b_{b;T_aK}\circ T_b(b_{a;K})$ is
$$T_bT_a(\varepsilon_{R,K})\circ T_b(c_{a;G_RK}^{-1})\circ c_{b;T_aG_RK}^{-1}.$$
Step 3 identifies its last two factors with $c_{ba;G_RK}^{-1}$. Both mixed paths consequently have transpose $S(\varepsilon_{A_n,K})\circ c_{d;G_{A_n}K}^{-1}$ under $I_{B_m}\dashv G_{B_m}$ and are equal. The pro-etale vertical maps in this recovery are exactly [lem-coef-finite-closed-shriek], not separately chosen isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 5

proof.text:
For the dualizing object use $F_R\dashv a_{X,R}^{\times}$ and its counit $\varepsilon_R:F_R\omega_R\to R$. Its unit-valued transpose defining $u_a$ is $T_a\varepsilon_R\circ C_{a;\omega_R}^{-1}$ followed by $T_aR\cong S$. Exactly the pasting formula of step 5, now for $C$ and the compact adjunction, gives for either two-arrow chain the transpose
$$T_bT_a\varepsilon_R\circ T_b(C_{a;\omega_R}^{-1})\circ C_{b;T_a\omega_R}^{-1},$$
followed by $T_bT_aR\cong U$. Step 4 and the unit compatibility of step 1 turn this into $T_{ba}\varepsilon_R\circ C_{ba;\omega_R}^{-1}$ and the canonical unit map. Hence both paths have the same transpose and the $u$ square commutes. At the vertical arrows these are precisely the isomorphisms of [lem-coef-finite-dualizing], whose statement specifies this transpose. Its hypotheses hold at $E$ with $(n,m)$ and at $L$ with $(en,em)$ by step 2.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 6

proof.text:
For internal Hom let $R\xrightarrow a S\xrightarrow b U$ be either chain, put $H_R=R\mathcal Hom_R(K,M)$, and let $w=v_{b;T_aK,T_aM}\circ T_b(v_{a;K,M})$. The defining transpose equation gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_U\circ(w\otimes1)=T_b\operatorname{ev}_S\circ(T_bv_a\otimes1)=T_bT_a\operatorname{ev}_R.$$
The first equality is the definition of $v_b$, precomposed with $T_bv_a\otimes1$; the second is the functorial image of the defining equation for $v_a$. Monoidality and composition compatibility in [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] supply exactly these identifications with both inputs extended. The closed tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] is injective, so $w$ is the single transpose for $ba$. Both chains have the same $d$ and the same pairing $S\operatorname{ev}_{A_n}$, proving the $v$ square. At each vertical arrow [thm-coef-finite-hom] identifies its comparison with exactly this transpose and proves invertibility; at the horizontal arrows [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change] does so for arbitrary inputs. Thus the calculation also applies to the dualizing and dual inputs of step 2.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 7

proof.text:
Expand $\beta_a=H_S(1,u_a)v_a$. Naturality of $v_b$ in its second input moves $T_bH_S(1,u_a)$ past $v_b$, so the composite Verdier comparison along $a,b$ is
$$H_U(1,u_b\circ T_bu_a)\,v_{b;T_aK,T_a\omega_R}\,T_bv_{a;K,\omega_R}.$$
Step 7 replaces the last two factors by the evaluation transpose for $ba$; step 6 replaces the first target map by $u_{ba}$. For the two chains these are identical, proving the $\beta$ square. The vertical identification is the finite Verdier comparison: [lem-coef-finite-target-change-coherence] applied to the quotient dualizing family gives exactly $H(1,u)v$, and [cor-coef-finite-verdier] is that evaluation-compatible comparison. The hypotheses on its target family are supplied by step 2 and the quotient cocycle in [lem-coef-finite-dualizing].

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 8

proof.text: For every edge $a:R\to S$, the defining equation of $v_a$ and $\beta_a=H(1,u_a)v_a$ give $\operatorname{ev}_{S,T_aK}(\beta_{a;K}\otimes1)=u_aT_a(\operatorname{ev}_{R,K})$. It holds also at $D_RK$, by step 2. Apply [lem-coef-finite-bidual-transpose] to these two equations: $\beta_{a;D_RK}T_a\delta_{R,K}=D_S(\beta_{a;K})\delta_{S,T_aK}$. Thus every edge respects the double-dual transpose, as well as evaluation. Pasting the edge equations and using the already proved $u,v,\beta$ squares proves preservation by the mixed square itself. The tensor symmetry is the signed symmetry in the cited lemma, which scalar extension preserves, so this argument does not suppress a sign or assume a biduality isomorphism.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3, quotient followed by extension: 9

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sf-finite-free-etale-proetale-transport] at levels $n$ and $m$: it identifies the horizontal $c,b,u,v,\beta$ with their named pro-etale maps, and identifies the quotient maps at $(n,m)$ over $E$ and $(en,em)$ over $L$. It expressly carries counit, evaluation and double-dual equations and the mixed square to the named square on the other site. Consequently applying the comparison functors to steps 3--9 proves all five pro-etale squares and their pairing compatibilities. The exceptional functor here is the transported constructible one. The etale closed vertical arrow was already identified in step 5, so no ambient unbounded pro-etale exceptional adjunction is invoked.
